text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall-nyc: Canary cluster for rollout r-2026-11-12 is seeing elevated 5xx across region us-east-1 and healthcheck failures. Current abort criteria met (error rate > 5% for 3m). https://console.redwood.ai/observability/rollouts/r-2026-11-12
oncall-nyc: taking it. oncall-nyc here.
Sanjay.patel: I'm on VPN, pulling logs now.
elaine.k: I see spike in 502/504 from edge LB -> canary backend, looks like timeouts + 502 from middleware.
marco: can you paste the probe path?
elaine.k: health check path is /live, status 200 expected but most responses are 500 with message "init failure: auth-middleware"
ops-bot: Recent deploy: service auth-gw@v2.3.1 rolled into canary 20% at 2026-11-12T03:14Z.
oncall-nyc: ok, checklist: 1) confirm customer impact 2) try emergency toggle 3) if no quick fix, abort rollout and rollback.
Sanjay.patel: quick metric: 6.4% 5xx across canary nodes last 5m, p95 latency +80ms. Affected: text-generation calls proxied through auth-gw.
elaine.k: stack traces from pods: ```
2026-11-12T03:20:15Z ERROR auth-middleware: user_lookup failed: upstream timeout
2026-11-12T03:20:15Z ERROR http: response 500 for /live
```
marco: thanks. Could be a change in new auth client (v2.3.1) that reorders async calls causing occasional upstream cancellation.
oncall-nyc: any chance to patch in place quickly?
Sanjay.patel: not safe to hotfix given async reorder. We'll do emergency toggle to stop canary traffic and then rollback. Recommend emergency flag flip to route 0% to canary.
elaine.k: product impacted: a subset of production traffic routed via feature flag ff.rollout.auth-gw. Customers in us-east-1 see intermittent failures, especially high QPS tenants. Ticketing note: #INC-5821 attached.
ops-bot: suggested command to abort rollout (console API):
```
curl -X POST "https://control.redwood.ai/api/v1/rollouts/r-2026-11-12/actions/abort" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"reason":"canary healthcheck failures: auth-gw 5xx"}'
```
oncall-nyc: executing emergency toggle first to confirm impact stops. Using flag service: `flags set ff.rollout.auth-gw.canary_percent 0`
Sanjay.patel: I'm watching logs.
elaine.k: flag flipped to 0. Observability link: https://console.redwood.ai/observability/services/auth-gw?window=5m
Sanjay.patel: immediate drop in 5xx to ~0.2% on non-canary nodes, canary nodes still draining but errors stop for new requests. Good sign.
oncall-nyc: OK we should abort and rollback to be safe. Initiating abort now.
ops-bot: running abort command...
ops-bot: Abort accepted, rollout r-2026-11-12 marked aborted by oncall-nyc. Rollback to last stable version v2.3.0 initiated.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Rollout aborted and rollback started. Notifying stakeholders and creating postmortem skeleton.
elaine.k: verifying recovery: canary cluster 5xx now back to baseline after drain. No ongoing customer alerts in PagerDuty.
marco: will keep watch for any residual flakiness, but looks contained.
oncall-nyc: oncall->sanjay handoff: I need someone to own the follow-up investigation. Sanjay, can you own RCA?
Sanjay.patel: I got it. Will pull git diff and run integration repro on staging reproducer. ETA for preliminary RCA in 2 hours.
oncall-nyc: handing off to night shift @oncall-eu. Summary for handoff: canary auth-gw v2.3.1 caused upstream timeouts -> /live healthcheck 500 -> abort criteria tripped (~6.4% 5xx) -> emergency flag toggled to 0 -> abort + rollback to v2.3.0 -> services recovering. Link to logs: https://console.redwood.ai/logs?query=auth-gw%20v2.3.1
oncall-nyc: next actions for oncall-eu: monitor rollback progress, confirm no customer-facing errors, and wait for Sanjay's RCA. If errors spike >3% for 10m, escalate to eng-runtime.
oncall-nyc: thanks all, transferring pager. :pray:
oncall-eu: acknowledged, taking over.
incident-bot: :clipboard: Incident created INC-5821, severity S2, assigned to eng-runtime and Sanjay.
Sanjay.patel: noted. Will include timeline, diff pointing to auth-client async fix, and suggested test to catch this in preflight (healthcheck mock for auth upstream delays).
elaine.k: adding customer comms draft to the ticket: short note about transient errors for some requests in us-east, rollback applied, monitoring.
marco: also flagging to release manager to block v2.3.1 until ESG tests pass.
ops-bot: action items logged: ["Abort rollout r-2026-11-12","Rollback to v2.3.0","Run canary isolation tests","Postmortem draft by Sanjay"]
Sanjay.patel: starting investigation now.
oncall-eu: will watch dashboards for next 2 hours and escalate if anything changes.
incident-bot: thread closed for active paging but remains for handoff discussion.
